paper_title: Strong constraints on decay and annihilation of dark matter from heating of gas-rich dwarf galaxies
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, ALP-photon coupling as plotted on y-axis of Fig. 4
notes: Paper (Wadekar & Wang, arXiv:2111.08025) sets new observed limits from gas heating of the Leo T dwarf galaxy on DM decay/annihilation, translated to ALP-photon coupling g_agamma in Fig. 4 (mass range ~5 eV-1 keV; strongest, world-leading region ~26.2 eV-1 keV). No numerical table is present in the provided text; the data_points above are RECONSTRUCTED from the paper's stated decay rate formula Gamma = m^3 g^2/(64pi), the cooling rate C_dot = 7e-30 GeV/cm^3/s, the FSM13 DM density profile, and the described photon opacity of Leo T (opaque for 13.6 < E_gamma < ~200 eV, sigma_PE ~ E^-3.5). They approximate the black 'Leo T gas temp.' curve of Fig. 4 (which dips to ~1e-15 GeV^-1 near a few hundred eV) but are not digitized figure values; treat as approximate (factor ~2-3 uncertainty). Limit rises steeply near the 2x13.6 eV=27.2 eV ionization threshold. The paper also constrains DM decay/annihilation to e+e-, Higgs-portal scalar mixing, sterile neutrino mixing, and dark neutron mixing (not encoded here; AxionPhoton chosen per Fig. 4, matching the pre-analysis hint). Not a haloscope; DM density is Leo T's halo profile, so dm_density_assumed is null. No explicit confidence level stated (conservative calorimetric bound); 0.95 assumed.
